high_consensus.description: Clear documentation defect with immediate execution risk: unrendered placeholders in commands and tables will mislead readers and break copy-paste validation flows. Very low effort, very high ROI.
This is a real gating ambiguity in Sprint 0 decision logic. Adding an explicit PASS/PASS-WITH-CONSTRAINTS/FAIL matrix is actionable and prevents cycle stalls.

Good architectural risk mitigation. The current rollback note is too shallow for a foundational component with many dependents. More detail is useful, though implementation/process overhead is moderate.
High-value security hardening. Sprint 0 collects live data before full redaction tooling exists, so a concrete manual/automated scrub process is essential to avoid credential/account leakage.
Strong medium-term maintainability improvement. Fixture evolution policy is important for keeping contract-smoke signal reliable as APIs change. Moderate complexity, solid payoff.
Domain-appropriate and highly actionable. Explicitly testing/documenting non-support for streaming avoids silent hangs and improves UX with minimal implementation cost.

blockers.concern: Auth direction is being locked from a very small survey sample (>=3), risking a strategic mismatch if users actually need SigV4/IAM first.
blockers.why_matters: If real production adopters require IAM-based auth, Bearer-only v1 may be unusable and force major redesign immediately after release.
blockers.location: Sprint 0 Acceptance Criteria G-S0-1; FR-4 deferred to Sprint 2 design-only
blockers.recommendation: Treat auth mode as a product risk gate: require stronger evidence (customer interviews/telemetry), and define explicit go/no-go criteria plus contingency scope for minimal SigV4 support.

blockers.concern: Centralized parser atomic refactor touches multiple Bash/Python callsites and can regress all providers, not just Bedrock.
blockers.why_matters: A parser edge-case regression can corrupt provider/model routing globally and break existing workflows despite Bedrock being opt-in.
blockers.recommendation: Use incremental rollout with compatibility shim and canary tests against all providers; require explicit regression suite for legacy model IDs before merge.

blockers.concern: Contract verification appears based on one account/region context and may not generalize across regions, accounts, or AWS partitions.
blockers.why_matters: Bedrock behavior can differ by region/profile availability and partition; a single-context fixture can mask failures for real users.
blockers.recommendation: Add multi-region and at least one secondary account validation matrix; explicitly document unsupported partitions (GovCloud/China) as constraints.

blockers.concern: PASS-WITH-CONSTRAINTS gate policy can allow Sprint 1 coding with unresolved contract ambiguity.
blockers.why_matters: If uncertainty is accepted too loosely, Sprint 1 builds against partial assumptions and may incur expensive rework across adapter, tests, and fixtures.
blockers.recommendation: Define strict allowed constraints per gate, plus mandatory mitigation tasks before Sprint 1 starts.

blockers.concern: Project-critical gates depend on a single maintainer Bedrock account and token, creating a hard single point of failure.
blockers.why_matters: Sprint 0 probes, Sprint 1 live tests, Sprint 2 E2E, and recurring smoke all require one operator-controlled account/secret. If access, quota, billing, or token rotation fails, delivery and validation halt.
blockers.location: Sprint 0/1/2 Dependencies sections; Task 1.10; Task 2.6; Task 2.E2E
blockers.recommendation: Add a backup test account/secret owner, documented break-glass credentials path, and non-blocking fallback validation mode when live Bedrock is unavailable.

blockers.concern: Secret-redaction strategy may miss transformed token leakage paths (partial, encoded, multiline, structured logs, CI debug output).
blockers.why_matters: A single missed leak in CI artifacts or audit logs compromises credentials and can create immediate security incident exposure.
blockers.location: Sprint 1 Task 1.6; Sprint 2 Task 2.6 security notes
blockers.recommendation: Add adversarial redaction tests (base64/url-encoded/chunked tokens), disable verbose HTTP logging by default, and run secret-scanning on produced artifacts.

blockers.concern: Timeline risk is high: 22 tasks plus E2E in 17 days includes core parser refactor, new provider integration, security controls, and CI automation.
blockers.why_matters: Underestimation can force quality cuts in testing/security hardening, increasing post-merge regressions.
blockers.location: Executive Summary timeline; Sprint 1 scope (LARGE, 10 tasks)
blockers.recommendation: Add schedule buffer, split must-have vs stretch tasks, and predefine de-scope candidates that do not compromise security or compatibility gates.
